intro_html: Keeps a history book for the records you choose to watch, per company: who created, changed, deleted, exported or opened each one, and what every changed value was before and after — so "who changed this supplier's bank account, and when?" becomes a question you can answer.

features.title: Watch Only What Matters
features.desc: Pick one kind of record at a time and tick exactly which of the five actions get recorded. Nothing is recorded until you switch a rule on.

features.title: Before and After, Side by Side
features.desc: Every change stores the old value next to the new one, on one screen you can search across every watched record at once.

features.title: A Copy of What Was Deleted
features.desc: Optionally keep the full contents of a record as it stood the moment it was deleted, so a removed record is still answerable.

features.title: See What Left the Building
features.desc: Spreadsheet exports are recorded too, with a button that reopens exactly the records that were exported.

features.title: One Person's Visit, Start to Finish
features.desc: Events are grouped into working sessions and the screen they came from, turning scattered entries into one readable story.

features.title: The Cost Is on the Screen
features.desc: Switching on view recording warns you first, in plain words: opening a list of 80 records records 80 events.

features.title: Clean-up Each Company Switches On
features.desc: Retention is off by default and set per company — nothing deletes audit evidence unless that company's admin says so.

features.title: Two Roles, Scoped by Company
features.desc: An Auditor who reads but never changes, and an Administrator who configures rules — both automatically limited to the companies they're already allowed to work in.

limitations: Only changes made through Odoo's ORM are recorded — direct SQL changes are not seen.
The company recorded is the user's current company at the time of the change, not the record's own company.
Binary/image and one-to-many fields aren't compared (their child records can be watched with their own rule).
Source Screen is best-effort, read from the browser address, and may be empty for API calls.
No approval, blocking, alerting or tamper-proof sealing — Audit Administrators can delete history.
